title: Impact of ACA Individual Mandate on Insurance Premiums

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID)**

This is a classic DID setup: we have treated regions (where the individual mandate was enforced) and control regions, observed before and after enforcement. The interaction term `treat_x_post` captures the causal effect of the mandate on log insurance premiums.

**Key Assumption: Parallel Trends** — In the absence of the mandate enforcement, treated and control regions would have followed the same trend in log insurance premiums. This is plausible if regions differ in levels but not in trajectory of premium growth prior to the policy.

**Expected mechanism:** The individual mandate forces healthier individuals into the risk pool, reducing adverse selection and theoretically lowering premiums. We expect a **negative** coefficient on the interaction term.

## 2. R Code

```r
# ============================================================
# DID Analysis: ACA Individual Mandate Impact on Premiums
# ============================================================

library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)
library(fixest)

# Load data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s41_data.csv")

cat("=== Data Summary ===\n")
str(df)
cat("\nDimensions:", nrow(df), "x", ncol(df), "\n")
cat("\nTreatment/Period Distribution:\n")
print(table(treated = df$treated, post = df$post))

cat("\n=== Group Means ===\n")
group_means <- aggregate(y ~ treated + post, data = df, FUN = mean)
print(group_means)

# Manual DID calculation
y00 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 0 & df$post == 0])
y01 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 0 & df$post == 1])
y10 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 1 & df$post == 0])
y11 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 1 & df$post == 1])
did_manual <- (y11 - y10) - (y01 - y00)
cat("\nManual DID estimate:", round(did_manual, 4), "\n")

# ============================================================
# Model 1: Basic DID via OLS
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== Model 1: Basic DID (OLS) ===\n")
m1 <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = df)
summary(m1)

# Robust standard errors (HC1)
cat("\n=== Model 1 with Robust SEs (HC1) ===\n")
coeftest_m1 <- coeftest(m1, vcov = vcovHC(m1, type = "HC1"))
print(coeftest_m1)

# ============================================================
# Model 2: DID with unit fixed effects (using fixest)
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== Model 2: DID with Unit Fixed Effects ===\n")
m2 <- feols(y ~ post + treat_x_post | unit_id, data = df)
summary(m2)

# ============================================================
# Model 3: DID with unit and period fixed effects
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== Model 3: Two-way Fixed Effects ===\n")
m3 <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = df)
summary(m3)

# ============================================================
# Model 4: Clustered standard errors at unit level
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== Model 4: DID with Cluster-Robust SEs (unit level) ===\n")
m4 <- feols(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = df, cluster = ~unit_id)
summary(m4)

# ============================================================
# Robustness Check 1: Parallel trends inspection
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== Robustness: Pre-treatment Means by Group ===\n")
pre_data <- df[df$post == 0, ]
pre_means <- aggregate(y ~ treated + period, data = pre_data, FUN = mean)
cat("Pre-period means by treated status and period:\n")
print(pre_means)

# ============================================================
# Robustness Check 2: Placebo test on pre-period
# ============================================================
cat("\n=== Robustness: Placebo Test (Pre-period only) ===\n")
pre_periods <- sort(unique(pre_data$period))
if (length(pre_periods) >= 2) {
  median_period <- median(pre_periods)
  pre_data$fake_post <- as.integer(pre_data$period > median_period)
  pre_data$fake_interact <- pre_data$treated * pre_data$fake_post
  placebo <- lm(y ~ treated + fake_post + fake_interact, data = pre_data)
  cat("Placebo DID coefficient:", round(coef(placebo)["fake_interact"], 4), "\n")
  cat("Placebo p-value:", round(summary(placebo)$coefficients["fake_interact", 4], 4), "\n")
} else {
  cat("Only one pre-period; placebo test not feasible.\n")
}

# ============================================================
# Summary of Results
# ============================================================
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("       SUMMARY OF DID ESTIMATES         \n")
cat("========================================\n")
cat("Manual DID:              ", round(did_manual, 4), "\n")
cat("OLS DID:                 ", round(coef(m1)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")
cat("Unit FE DID:             ", round(coef(m2)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")
cat("Two-way FE DID:          ", round(coef(m3)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")
cat("Clustered SE DID:        ", round(coef(m4)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")
cat("========================================\n")
cat("\nInterpretation: The DID coefficient represents the\n")
cat("causal effect of mandate enforcement on log premiums.\n")
cat("A coefficient of X means premiums changed by ~X*100%.\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Expected sign:** **Negative** coefficient on `treat_x_post`. The individual mandate reduces adverse selection by bringing healthier individuals into the insurance pool, which should lower average premiums in treated regions relative to controls.

**Expected magnitude:** A coefficient in the range of **-0.10 to -0.50** on the log scale, corresponding to roughly a 10–40% reduction in premiums. The exact magnitude depends on the simulation's data-generating process, but given that this is a stylized dataset with 150 observations and a clear DID structure, I expect a statistically significant effect.

**Robustness expectations:**
- The placebo test should yield an **insignificant** coefficient, supporting the parallel trends assumption.
- Results should be consistent across specifications (basic OLS, unit FE, TWFE), with the DID point estimate remaining stable. Standard errors may widen with clustering, but significance should hold if the effect is meaningfully sized.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare regions before and after mandate enforcement.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The enforcement of the mandate led to a decrease in insurance premiums.
